transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-06-30 14:00 PDT | Duration: ~47 mins | Attendees: Maya Chen, Luis Ortega, Ava Brooks (Redwood) - Omar Patel, Zoe Kim, Priya Srinivasan, Ben Foster (Pelagia)

Summary: quick sync to align on integration approach. Primary ask: how to route calls through a company gateway, LangChain adapters, token limits, and what observability hooks Redwood exposes. Pelagia evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, can you hear me ok?
[00:05] Priya: yes yes, sounds good.
[00:08] Maya: sweet. quick agenda, we'll do 10 minutes of background from you, 25 on integration patterns, and then 10 for next steps and security Qs. does that work?
[00:18] Omar: works for us. we mostly want to confirm the gateway approach - we have an internal proxy that handles auth and metrics and we'd like to keep it in the path.
[00:27] Luis: perfect. i can sketch how teams usually wire the SDK or a LangChain/LlamaIndex layer behind a gateway. also cover rate quotas and observability hooks.

[02:10] Zoe: quick context - Pelagia runs a central API gateway (kong-ish) and we do tenant-level routing. our ML infra team builds feature services that call LLM endpoints. latency for our realtime assistant must be <250ms p50 token gen ideally.
[02:30] Ben: from security, we'll need KMS integration, audit logs, and SSO. also we cannot send PII outside certain regions, so data residency is a must.
[02:45] Maya: noted. Pelagia, are you leaning Dedicated or Private to start?
[02:50] Priya: leaning Dedicated because we don't want to manage infra ourselves yet, but need network isolation and keys in our KMS. open to Private if Dedicated can't meet residency/keys.

[05:00] Luis: architecture options — three common patterns: 1) client services call Redwood SDK directly (hosted API); 2) central gateway/proxy forwards to Redwood (adds auth, quotas, header inject); 3) on-prem/private where a local Redwood endpoint lives in your VPC. For your gateway pattern we recommend (2) with token exchange so the gateway holds SSO and mints short-lived tokens for Redwood.
[05:30] Omar: can you elaborate on token exchange? we don't want to share long lived keys in code.
[05:35] Luis: yep. gateway calls your identity provider to assert user/tenant and then requests a short-lived session token from Redwood using our token minting API. gateway then attaches the token to outbound requests. we can also do signed JWTs with headers if that's easier.

[07:00] Zoe: any examples for LangChain/LlamaIndex usage? our engineers use LangChain for orchestration and LlamaIndex for vector retrieval flows. we want to keep embeddings in our vector DB but call Redwood for encoder/generation.
[07:20] Luis: common: use Redwood's client SDK as the LLM backend in LangChain via a simple adapter. for LlamaIndex you typically implement the query transform to call Redwood's embeddings endpoint then persist vectors to your DB. we have sample adapters — we'll share repo links. note: streaming can be used for chat UIs and LangChain chains that benefit from partial outputs.
[07:50] Maya: small caveat — sometimes LlamaIndex names or function calls get transcribed weird in logs, so patching name mappings helps.

[10:15] Omar: about rate limits — we need per-tenant quotas and burst protection. we want to ensure a single runaway job doesn't blow up costs or latency. can Redwood enforce per-api-key and per-tenant quotas when calls come from our gateway?
[10:30] Miguel (speaker misattributed earlier): yes, Redwood supports per-key and per-route quotas. if gateway mints short-lived tokens per tenant we can apply quotas at token level. we also have configurable burst windows and graceful 429 behavior with retry-after headers.
[10:45] Priya: how deterministic are the 429s? we need to ensure critical flows failover to a lower-cost model rather than hard error.
[10:55] Luis: you can do automated fallback policies in Redwood Console — e.g., on 429 or capacity issues route to a smaller/cheaper model or regional fallback. that adds complexity but keeps service up.

[13:00] Zoe: observability — what hooks do you expose? we need traces tied to our request IDs, per-route latency, token counts, and cost breakdowns.
[13:15] Luis: we emit per-request metrics: tokens consumed, latency, model version, and error codes. we integrate with Datadog/NewRelic via metrics export, and provide trace context propagation (we support W3C traceparent headers). You can forward your request-id from the gateway and we'll include it in logs.
[13:38] Ben: how long do logs/usage events persist? our compliance wants 12 months of audit trails.
[13:45] Maya: default retention is 90 days, but enterprise tiers can request longer retention as an add-on — check the compliance pack. we'll include the retention add-on pricing.

[16:20] Omar: on the SDK: does Redwood's SDK add retries and batching by default? our services sometimes send many short prompts and we want efficient token usage.
[16:35] Luis: SDK has optional batching and automatic prefix KV caching for session flows. batching is opt-in and optimized for throughput. you'll want to tune batch window vs latency. SDK also supports streaming and callback hooks so you can measure partial token latency.
[16:55] Zoe: you mentioned KV cache — are there gotchas with chat state? our engineers worried about cache staleness across replicas.
[17:10] Luis: the runtime manages KV cache affinity per session, but if you use Dedicated pools we keep session affinity stable; in Hosted there's some best practices to pin conversation IDs. sometimes docs call it K V cash and that confuses folks.

[19:00] Priya: let's talk costs quickly — demo showed hosted is cheaper per initial setup, Dedicated is better for predictable high throughput. do you have a rule of thumb?
[19:12] Maya: rough rule: if you're >X million tokens/month with strict latency needs, Dedicated usually reduces unit cost and gives predictable SLA. We'll send concrete pricing examples for your workloads.

[21:00] Omar: we also plan to use a gateway to rewrite prompts for safety filters before sending them to Redwood. can we run pre-processing in gateway then call Redwood? any latency concern?
[21:18] Luis: that's a common pattern. keep pre-processing cheap — if you call Redwood for safety checks you'll add round trips. some customers run lightweight safety checks in gateway and run deeper evals asynchronously.

[23:30] Zoe: on embeddings: we want to run embedding generation in region X and keep vectors on our DB. can Redwood ensure the embeddings endpoint and model stay in region?
[23:45] Maya: yes, for Dedicated/Private you can choose region and we support data residency constraints. Hosted API can be region-constrained depending on account setup; we'll confirm specifics in the security whitepaper.

[25:40] Ben: security nitty-gritty — are audit logs tamper-evident? do you support HSM for key wrapping?
[25:50] Luis: we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS/Azure KeyVault/GCP KMS) for envelope keys; HSM-backed KMS is supported. audit logs are exported and we can enable append-only retention in Private deployments. for hosted, we have standard audit trails but can export them to your logging accounts.

[28:10] Omar: about pilot — we want to run a 2-week pilot comparing hosted vs dedicated for our assistant. what do we need to provide?
[28:22] Maya: we'll ask you to provide a representative prompt set, traffic pattern, and latency SLO. Luis will provide a benchmark template. Redwood will provision a small Dedicated ring for the pilot and share runbook.

[30:05] Zoe: any SDK pitfalls with LangChain in async flows? our chains are highly parallel.
[30:15] Luis: be careful with naive concurrency — SDK has connection pooling and rate limit back-pressure, but LangChain parallel calls can saturate. recommend a client-side semaphore to control concurrency and use batching when possible. we'll share sample code.

[32:40] Priya: we'd like to centralize cost attribution per product team — can Redwood export token-level billing broken by API key or path?
[32:52] Maya: yes we have per-token cost breakdowns in Console and via export APIs. you can tag keys by team and pull cost reports daily.

[34:10] Ben: any concerns about PII in embeddings? we plan to scrub some fields but need guidance.
[34:20] Luis: best practice: do deterministic PII masking before embedding. also you can opt out of retention or set ephemeral flags for certain calls. for stricter needs use Private where logs don't leave your VPC.

[36:00] Omar: let's discuss the gateway header mapping — we want to inject user-id and tenant-id, but not the internal service token. is there a recommended header set?
[36:12] Luis: recommended headers: x-pelagia-tenant, x-pelagia-user, x-request-id. Redwood reads x-request-id and traceparent. avoid sending internal auth tokens in plaintext; use token exchange so the gateway sends only short-lived Redwood tokens in authorization header.

[38:40] Zoe: what about webhook callbacks or async evals for long-running responses?
[38:50] Luis: we have async job APIs and webhooks. For large generation tasks it's common to request an async job; Redwood will POST to your callback URL when ready and include request metadata and cost. callbacks can be signed.

[41:00] Priya: ok last security thing — SSO for the Console. can we bind RBAC to our SAML groups?
[41:08] Maya: yes, enterprise accounts support SAML/SSO and group-based RBAC. we'll need your IdP metadata.

[42:30] Omar: final recap?
[42:34] Maya: recap — Redwood to send Dedicated pricing + burst options, SOC2 whitepaper, SDK adapter links for LangChain/LlamaIndex, and a benchmark template. Pelagia to share prompt set and compliance questions. Plan: schedule SE perf deep-dive next week.
[42:50] Priya: sounds good.
[43:10] Ben: thanks all.
[43:20] Zoe: quick note — please include an example gateway token exchange flow, that's high value.
[43:26] Luis: will do.
[43:30] Maya: ok we'll follow up via email and slack, thanks everyone.
[43:35] Priya: bye.

Action items (read back):
- Maya: send Dedicated pricing + security paper (due 2025-07-02)
- Luis: benchmark template and sample adapter repos (due 2025-07-04)
- Ben (Pelagia): send compliance questions and KMS/IAM requirements (due 2025-07-03)

End of transcript.
